definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., rules, orders, official statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva cessou durante a tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain stopped during the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva cessou durante a noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain stopped during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coloquei as frutas na cesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the fruit in the basket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um cesto de frutas no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a basket of fruit at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cevada é usada para fazer cerveja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Barley is used to make beer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou colocar água na chaleira para fazer chá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put water in the kettle to make tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chama da vela apagou-se com o vento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle flame went out with the wind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me chama todo dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She calls me every day.

definitions.note: Often used for a phone call; in school/work contexts it can also mean a roll call (attendance check).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Recebi uma chamada da minha mãe ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a call from my mom last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "chamar"; used to agree with a feminine noun (e.g., "a reunião foi chamada").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A reunião foi chamada para amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was called for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "chamada".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Recebi duas chamadas hoje de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received two calls this morning.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle of "chamar"; often used in passive voice (e.g., "foram chamadas")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As meninas foram chamadas pelo professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls were called by the teacher.

definitions.note: Often used for phone calls or a call/request for service (e.g., a support ticket).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Recebi um chamado do suporte técnico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a call from technical support.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi chamado para a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was called to the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro foi chamado de Luna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was named Luna.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural (they/you all call).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles me chamam todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They call me every day.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós). Can also mean “we name” or “we invite” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chamamos o médico agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We call the doctor now.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “chamar” (used with “estar” or to mean “while/by calling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chamando o médico agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calling the doctor now.

definitions.note: Often used for calling someone on the phone, calling out to someone, or calling someone/something by a name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou chamar a minha mãe mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call my mom later.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chamar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chamaram um táxi depois do show.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called a taxi after the show.

definitions.note: Often used after conjunctions like "quando" (when) or "se" (if), meaning something like “when/if they call…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chamarem você, pode entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they call you, you can come in.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "chamar" (used for hypothetical situations or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chamaria um táxi, mas não tenho dinheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would call a taxi, but I don’t have any money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chamas estavam muito altas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flames were very high.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação habitual/contínua no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu era criança, eu chamava a minha avó todos os domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I called my grandma every Sunday.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all called; they/you all were calling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chamavam o professor de "doutor".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called the professor "doctor".

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used as an affirmative formal command: “call!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você me chame amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you call me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu te chamei ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you last night.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês / eles / elas) form of "chamar"; also used for affirmative commands to "vocês" (e.g., "Chamem o médico!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que chamem o médico a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they call the doctor in time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saiu fumaça pela chaminé da casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoke came out through the house’s chimney.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu). Often used to say your name: “Eu me chamo …” = “My name is …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chamo o garçom quando preciso de ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call the waiter when I need help.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chamar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me chamou ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She called me last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos brindar com champanhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s toast with champagne.

definitions.note: Colloquial spoken form of "chamar" (often used in Brazil), typically before a pronoun: "chamá ele" = "chamar ele".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou chamá você mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call you later.

definitions.native: we called, we used to call
definitions.note: Imperfect past: can mean a habitual action in the past (“used to call”) or an ongoing/background action (“were calling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando éramos crianças, chamávamos a nossa avó todos os domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we used to call our grandmother every Sunday.

definitions.native: -chan (Japanese honorific suffix; term of endearment, often for children or close friends)
definitions.note: Used in Portuguese mostly in Japanese-culture contexts (anime/manga fandom) as a borrowed suffix after a name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Mei-chan é muito fofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mei-chan is very cute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tive a chance de falar com ela ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the chance to talk to her yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem boas chances de passar no exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good chance of passing the exam.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "chantagear" (used like “blackmailing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está me chantageando para eu fazer o que ele quer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is blackmailing me so that I do what he wants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou chantagear o colega para conseguir dinheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to blackmail his coworker to get money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chantageou o colega para conseguir dinheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He blackmailed his colleague to get money.

definitions.note: Informal/slang, usually about being under the influence of drugs (sometimes alcohol).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está chapado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is high.

definitions.note: Often used for something very flat or pressed flat (e.g., metal, a tire, a surface).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pneu está chapado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire is flat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou um chapéu novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a new hat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os chapéus estão na prateleira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hats are on the shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças adoram charadas na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids love riddles at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muito charme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of charm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acendeu um charuto depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lit a cigar after dinner.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "chato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele barulho é muito chata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is very annoying.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "chato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A palestra ficou chata depois de um tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lecture got boring after a while.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou chateada com o comentário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got upset about the comment.

definitions.note: Often used to describe feeling upset or bothered (can mean “bummed” in casual contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chateado com o que aconteceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m upset about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi muito chato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very boring.

definitions.note: Plural form; used to describe people/things (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses filmes são muito chatos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those movies are very boring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdi a chave de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the house key.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, "chave" is also commonly used in tool names, like "chave de fenda" (screwdriver) and "chave inglesa" (adjustable wrench).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem uma chave para apertar esse parafuso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a wrench to tighten this screw?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um chaveiro novo para as chaves de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new keychain for my house keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chaveiro abriu a porta em poucos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The locksmith opened the door in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Plural of "chave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onde estão as chaves do carro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are the car keys?

definitions.note: Also commonly means “we check (something) out” in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Checamos os documentos antes de assinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We check the documents before signing.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese; in some contexts you can also use "verificar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou checar o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check the email before leaving.

definitions.note: Loanword from English; in Portuguese this is often written as “cheque”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um check.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Nationality/demonym; can also be used as an adjective (“Czech”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O checo mora em Praga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Czech man lives in Prague.

definitions.note: Informal; from the verb “checar” (common in Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele checou o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He checked the email before leaving.

definitions.note: In Brazil, very common meaning is “boss” in workplaces. It can also mean “chief” (leader) more generally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou falar com o meu chefe depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll talk to my boss after lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu chefe chega cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss arrives early every day.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "chegar"; can also be used for "you arrive/come" with "você".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus chega às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus arrives at eight.

definitions.note: Common as an interjection meaning “that’s enough/stop.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chega, eu já entendi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough, I already understood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chegada do ônibus foi atrasada por causa do trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus’s arrival was delayed because of traffic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tinha chegado cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had arrived early.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in the expression “amigos chegados” (“close friends”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são amigos chegados desde a escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been close friends since school.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "chegar" (they arrive / you all arrive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegam às oito todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrive at eight every day.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "chegar" with "we" (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegamos ao aeroporto bem cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived at the airport very early.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "chegar"; often used after "estar" to mean "is/are arriving" or "is/are coming".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chegando em casa agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m arriving home now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chego em casa às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get home at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegaram cedo ao aeroporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrived early at the airport.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive of "chegar" used after certain conjunctions/prepositions; typically means "(for them) to arrive" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos esperar eles chegarem antes de começar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to wait for them to arrive before starting.

definitions.native: we will arrive, we will get there
definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaremos ao aeroporto às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will arrive at the airport at eight.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "chegar" (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegaria mais cedo se não houvesse trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would arrive earlier if there weren’t traffic.

definitions.note: Often used after time/condition words like "quando" (when) or "se" (if), referring to a future situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chegarmos, eu te ligo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrive, I'll call you.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive; often used after prepositions like "para" (in order to) or "até" (until).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos sair cedo para chegarmos a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's leave early so we can arrive on time.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O trem chegará às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will arrive at eight.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você). Often used with "a" (e.g., chegar a algum lugar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chegará ao aeroporto cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will get to the airport early.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "chegar"; used after expressions like "if" or "I wanted that" to talk about a hypothetical/desired past situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ele chegasse mais cedo, nós sairíamos juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he arrived earlier, we would go out together.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "chegar" (used after triggers like "se", "queria que", "era importante que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu queria que eles chegassem cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted them to arrive early.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; common in European Portuguese and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaste tarde ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You arrived late yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegava em casa por volta das seis todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived home around six every day.

definitions.native: I arrive, I get (to), I reach
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chego em casa às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get home at six.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it arrived; you arrived; also used for “you” in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chegou em casa tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He arrived home late.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "chegar" (also used for formal commands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você chegue cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you arrive early.

definitions.note: First-person singular in the past (pretérito perfeito) of "chegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheguei em casa às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got home at eight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) and also the affirmative command for vocês.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cheguem a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they arrive on time.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A garrafa está cheia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is full.

definitions.note: Used especially in the expression “cheia do rio” (river flood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cheia do rio alagou a cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flood flooded the city.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “cheio”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As garrafas estão cheias de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottles are full of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O copo está cheio de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is full of water.

definitions.note: Used as a noun; often refers to the state of being full or the “full” side/part (e.g., in contrasts like “the full and the empty”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tanque, o cheio indica o nível máximo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the tank, the full mark indicates the maximum level.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "cheio" (used with masculine plural nouns, or mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os copos estão cheios de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cups are full of water.

definitions.note: Usually used with "a" + noun: "cheira a" = "smells like".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo cheira a mofo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells like mold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro está cheirando o chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sniffing the ground.

definitions.note: Can mean either to sense an odor (with your nose) or to have a smell (give off an odor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo está a cheirar mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells bad.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cozinha cheirava a pão fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen smelled like fresh bread.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "cheirar" (also used in some formal commands, e.g., "Cheire isto.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu cheire melhor amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I smell better tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu cheiro as flores no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smell the flowers in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que cheiro bom de café!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a nice smell of coffee!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto dos cheiros das flores na primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the smells of the flowers in spring.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (for você), meaning “check/verify.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheque as informações antes de confirmar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the information before confirming.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, people often write "cheque" as "cheque"; in English, "cheque" is the British spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um cheque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chequei meu e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked my email before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem um chiclete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any chewing gum?

definitions.note: Plural of "chifre".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O veado tem chifres grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deer has big horns.

definitions.note: Often refers to casual open footwear (like flip-flops).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não esqueça de levar os chinelos para a piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to bring your flip-flops to the pool.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é chinesa e mora no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Chinese and lives in Brazil.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used for women or feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As estudantes chinesas falam português muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese students speak Portuguese very well.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of the adjective (also used for mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os restaurantes chineses desta rua são muito bons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese restaurants on this street are very good.

definitions.note: Plural of "chinês"; can refer to a group of Chinese people (often men/mixed group depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos chineses morando aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Chinese people living here.

definitions.note: Can describe something from China or the Chinese language; as an adjective it agrees in gender/number with the noun it modifies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Chinese at school.

definitions.note: Can refer to a Chinese person or, in some contexts, the Chinese language; here it’s used as a noun for a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chinês mora aqui há dois anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese man has lived here for two years.

definitions.note: As a noun, it can also mean the Chinese language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou aprendendo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Chinese at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estava muito chique na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked very chic at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chiqueiro fica atrás do celeiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pigsty is behind the barn.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou chocada com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was shocked by the news.

definitions.note: Often used for people reacting to surprising or upsetting news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei chocado com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was shocked by the news.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles ficaram chocados com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were shocked by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia foi chocante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was shocking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is committing a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a serious mistake.

definitions.note: Often used as “they committed” (or “you all committed,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles cometeram um erro grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They made a serious mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele cometeu um erro grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed a serious mistake.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of “cometer”. Often used with nouns like “um erro” (a mistake) or “um crime” (a crime).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake when filling out the form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crime was committed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu cometo erros às vezes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make mistakes sometimes.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "comer" (to eat).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project has already been started.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Classes start at eight.

definitions.note: Can also mean “we started/began” depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we start the project.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “começar”; often used with “estar” to mean “to be starting.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos começar agora.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They started the project yesterday.

definitions.native: we will start, we will begin

definitions.native: (for us) to start, (for us) to begin

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor começarmos agora.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of "começar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A aula começará às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class will start at eight.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã, eles começarão o trabalho cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, they will start the work early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu começo o trabalho às nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I start work at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O começo do filme é muito bom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The beginning of the movie is very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme começou muito tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie started very late.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "comer" for "eu" (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem eu comi pizza no jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ate pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "comer"; used for ongoing/repeated past actions ("was eating", "used to eat").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando você ligou, eu comia um sanduíche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you called, I was eating a sandwich.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "comer"; often used with an auxiliary (e.g., in the passive voice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pizza já foi comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pizza has already been eaten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A comida está deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food is delicious.

definitions.note: Plural of "comida".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As comidas do restaurante são muito boas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant’s meals are very good.

definitions.note: Past participle of "comer"; often used with "ter/haver" to form compound tenses, or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu já tinha comido quando eles chegaram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already eaten when they arrived.

definitions.note: Used after the preposition “com” (you say “comigo”, not *“com mim”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você quer vir comigo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to come with me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os comissários aprovaram a nova regra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commissioners approved the new rule.

definitions.note: In air travel, “comissários (de bordo)” refers to the cabin crew; in Brazil, “comissário” is often used for a male flight attendant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os comissários pediram para todos apertarem o cinto de segurança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight attendants asked everyone to fasten their seat belts.

definitions.note: Often used for an official group/committee formed to deal with a specific issue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A comissão vai apresentar o relatório amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commission will present the report tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela faz parte de uma comissão da escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is part of a school committee.

definitions.note: In business, can mean a percentage/fee earned on sales.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O vendedor recebe comissão por cada venda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesperson earns a commission for each sale.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O comitê vai decidir amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee will decide tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st-person singular (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu como arroz todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat rice every day.

definitions.note: Used to indicate a role or function (e.g., a job or position).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha como enfermeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works as a nurse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Como você está?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?

definitions.note: Used to make comparisons or give examples.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele corre como um atleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He runs like an athlete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela canta como um anjo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sings like an angel.

definitions.note: Used to introduce an indirect question or explain the way something is done.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sei como explicar isso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know how to explain that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O discurso dela foi comovente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her speech was moving.

definitions.note: Usually refers to being emotionally affected (not physical movement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A história comoveu muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story moved a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sentiu compaixão pelas pessoas que perderam a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt compassion for the people who lost their home.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic partner or life partner; can also mean a companion or colleague depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela veio com o companheiro dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came with her partner.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles viajaram como companheiros por toda a Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They traveled as companions throughout Europe.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of a business/company or organization; for “company” meaning “being with someone,” Portuguese also commonly uses “companhia” in expressions like “em companhia de.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha em uma companhia de tecnologia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works at a technology company.

definitions.note: Refers to being with someone or the presence of others (not necessarily a business).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Obrigado pela sua companhia hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your company today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As companhias aéreas cancelaram vários voos hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The airlines cancelled several flights today.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of people you spend time with (your companions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela viajou com duas companhias muito divertidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She traveled with two very fun companions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela compara os preços antes de comprar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She compares prices before buying.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle; agrees with a feminine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cidade é pequena, comparada com São Paulo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is small compared to São Paulo.

definitions.note: Past participle of "comparar"; often used with "a" (to) or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comparado com o ano passado, este mês foi melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compared to last year, this month was better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou comparar os dois preços antes de comprar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to compare the two prices before buying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A comparação entre os dois planos é fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The comparison between the two plans is easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu comparei os dois preços antes de comprar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I compared the two prices before buying.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, especially meaning to show up in person (e.g., for an appointment, meeting, or court date).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele teve de comparecer ao tribunal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to appear in court.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles compareceram à reunião às nove.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They showed up at the meeting at nine.

definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você) of "comparecer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela compareceu à reunião no horário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed up to the meeting on time.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they/you all share).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles compartilham fotos da viagem com a família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They share photos from the trip with the family.

definitions.note: Present tense ("we share") or simple past ("we shared"), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós compartilhamos a mesma opinião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We share the same opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode compartilhar este arquivo comigo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you share this file with me?

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação contínua/habitual no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela compartilhava fotos da viagem com a família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She used to share photos from the trip with her family.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu compartilhei a foto com os meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shared the photo with my friends.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu compartilho este artigo com você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I share this article with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela compartilhou a notícia com a família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shared the news with her family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O aumento compensa o esforço extra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The raise compensates for the extra effort.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally to mean “it’s worth it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mesmo com trânsito, compensa ir de carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even with traffic, it’s worth going by car.

definitions.native: to compensate, to make up for
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou compensar o tempo que perdi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make up for the time I lost.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma profissional muito competente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very competent professional.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The competitors arrived early for the event.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai competir no campeonato no próximo mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to compete in the championship next month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mercado de tecnologia é muito competitivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technology market is very competitive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A competição foi muito difícil este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The competition was very difficult this year.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As competições começam amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The competitions start tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A lista está completa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The list is complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou completamente cansado hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m completely tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso completar este formulário hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to complete this form today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Completei o formulário ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completed the form last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório está completo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is complete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela completou o curso ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She completed the course yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A situação é complexa, mas vamos resolver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is complex, but we’re going to solve it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este problema é muito complexo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This problem is very complex.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso complica tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That complicates everything.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A situação ficou muito complicada depois da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation became very complicated after the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a situation or problem that’s hard to deal with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta parte do exercício está complicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This part of the exercise is difficult.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As instruções estão complicadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are complicated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O exercício foi mais complicado do que eu esperava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exercise was more complicated than I expected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os horários estão complicados esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schedules are complicated this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso vai complicar tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That will complicate everything.

definitions.note: Plural of "componente".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os componentes do computador chegaram hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer components arrived today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se comporta muito bem na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaves very well at school.

definitions.note: Often used with quantities or capacity (how many people/things a space can hold).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este carro comporta cinco pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car fits five people.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe someone (especially a child) who behaves properly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu filho ficou muito comportado na escola hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son was very well-behaved at school today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles não se comportam bem na aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They don’t behave well in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O comportamento dele mudou depois da escola nova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior changed after the new school.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: "se comportando" = "behaving".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças estão se comportando bem na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are behaving well at school.

definitions.note: Used to say a place/thing has capacity for something or someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O auditório está comportando 300 pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The auditorium is holding 300 people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças precisam se comportar na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children need to behave at school.

definitions.note: Often used with "caber" as a near-synonym in the sense of having enough space/capacity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta mala não vai comportar todas as minhas roupas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase won’t hold all my clothes.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after 'que') or as a command (imperative for você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ele se comporte bem na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he behaves well at the party.

definitions.note: Used when talking about capacity (how much something can fit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que a caixa comporte todos os livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that the box holds all the books.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for negative commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês se comportem bem na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you behave well at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se comportou muito bem na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaved very well in the meeting.

definitions.note: Commonly used to mean that something has enough space/capacity for something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A caixa comportou todos os livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The box contained all the books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O compositor escreveu uma música nova para o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composer wrote a new piece of music for the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os compositores escreveram músicas para o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composers wrote music for the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A composição da música é muito bonita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composition of the song is very beautiful.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “composição química” (chemical composition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a composição deste produto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the makeup of this product?

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "compor"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "é composta por" = "is made up of").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A equipe é composta por cinco pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team is made up of five people.

definitions.note: Past participle of "compor"; often used in expressions like "ser composto por" (to be made up of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O curso é composto por oito aulas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course is made up of eight lessons.

definitions.note: Often used in science, especially for a chemical compound.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A água é um composto formado por hidrogênio e oxigênio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cientistas estudam compostos químicos no laboratório.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists study chemical compounds in the laboratory.

definitions.note: Often said as "composto orgânico" in gardening contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Colocámos compostos no jardim para melhorar a terra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put compost in the garden to improve the soil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela manteve a compostura durante toda a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept her composure throughout the whole meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A compra foi feita ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The purchase was made yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela compra pão todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She buys bread every day.

definitions.note: Past participle of "comprar"; often used with "ser" in the passive or with "ter/haver" in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro foi comprado ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car was bought yesterday.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "comprar" (used with "eles/elas/vocês" or a plural subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles compram pão na padaria todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They buy bread at the bakery every day.

definitions.note: Can mean either present tense (“we buy”) or simple past/preterite (“we bought”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós compramos frutas no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We buy fruit at the market.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "comprar"; often used to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está comprando pão na padaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is buying bread at the bakery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero comprar pão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to buy bread.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito): “they bought” or “you (plural, formal) bought.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles compraram pão e leite no supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bought bread and milk at the supermarket.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã comprarei um presente para a minha mãe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will buy a gift for my mother.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu compraria esse livro se fosse mais barato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would buy that book if it were cheaper.

definitions.note: Conditional (they/you all/you formal plural).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had more money, they would buy a bigger house.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of "comprar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela comprará um carro novo no próximo ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will buy a new car next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou fazer as compras no supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to do the shopping at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compraste um livro ontem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you buy a book yesterday?
