definitions.note: Usually means a calendar date (day/month/year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a data do seu aniversário?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the date of your birthday?

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: “dados”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos proteger os dados dos clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to protect customer data.

definitions.note: Plural of "data" (in the calendar sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso confirmar as datas da viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to confirm the dates of the trip.

definitions.note: Plural of "data"; in Portuguese, "data" is usually singular and "dados" is the plural when meaning "information".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cientistas analisaram as datas do experimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scientists analyzed the data from the experiment.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/repeated action in the past) of “dar” (“to give”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sempre me dava um chocolate quando eu era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always gave me a chocolate when I was a child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira a chave daí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the key from there, please.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a consequence or next step in speech (similar to “so/then”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Daí eu percebi que estava errado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Then I realized I was wrong.

definitions.note: Very common preposition. It often contracts with articles (e.g., de + o = do, de + a = da).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é de Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is from Portugal.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("debaixo de") to mean "under/beneath" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gato está debaixo da mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is under the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O debate foi muito interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The debate was very interesting.

definitions.note: Used for the head of a faculty/school at a university (not a cathedral dean).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A decano da Faculdade de Direito falou na cerimónia de abertura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dean of the Law School spoke at the opening ceremony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é uma pessoa decente e honesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a decent and honest person.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine), depending on what it describes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são pessoas decentes e trabalhadoras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are decent, hardworking people.

definitions.note: Often confused with English "deception"—it means "disappoints," not "deceives."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso me decepciona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That disappoints me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei decepcionado com o resultado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was disappointed with the result.

definitions.note: Masculine plural (can also be used for a mixed-gender group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles ficaram decepcionados com o resultado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were disappointed with the result.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O final do filme foi decepcionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie was disappointing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se esforçou muito, mas o resultado final a decepcionou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tried very hard, but the final result disappointed her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senti uma grande decepção quando o show foi cancelado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt a great disappointment when the show was canceled.

definitions.note: Formal command (você) or present subjunctive form of “decidir” (used after expressions like “I hope that…”, “it’s important that…”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você decida hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you decide today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decide amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decides tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidi ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está decidido a terminar o curso este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is determined to finish the course this year.

definitions.note: Past participle of "decidir"; often used in passive or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Já está decidido: vamos viajar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s already decided: we’re traveling tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de conversar, decidimos sair mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After talking, we decided to leave earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso decidir hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to decide today.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles decidiram ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to stay home today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (future tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidirá amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will decide tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) preterite (past simple).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu decidiste mudar de emprego no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You decided to change jobs last year.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person singular: “he/she/it decided” or “you (formal) decided”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu viajar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to travel tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa foi uma decisão difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a difficult decision.

definitions.note: Plural of "decisão".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos tomar decisões importantes hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to make important decisions today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O imposto já foi declarado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tax has already been declared.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., official statements, taxes, customs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele declarou tudo o que sabia à polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stated everything he knew to the police.

definitions.note: Often used for an official statement or document.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de uma declaração do banco para o visto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a statement from the bank for the visa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Declaro que li e aceito os termos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I declare that I have read and accept the terms.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form: “(he/she/you formal) declared.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela declarou que não sabia de nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She declared that she didn’t know anything.

definitions.note: Used for planes/aircraft; also used figuratively (e.g., a project taking off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O avião vai decolar às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to take off at eight.

definitions.note: Used for an airplane (or other aircraft) taking off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decolaremos em dez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take off in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O avião decolou às oito horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off at eight o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou decorando a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m decorating the living room for the party.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, decorar is also commonly used to mean “to memorize” (e.g., words, lines, facts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está decorando as falas para a peça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s memorizing her lines for the play.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai decorar a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to decorate the living room for the party.

definitions.native: to memorize, to learn by heart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso decorar este poema para amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to memorize this poem for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decorou a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decorated the living room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele decorou o poema em uma tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He memorized the poem in one afternoon.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma professora muito dedicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very dedicated teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito dedicado ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very dedicated to his work.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (e.g., "dedicar algo a alguém/alguma coisa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu dedicar mais tempo aos estudos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to devote more time to her studies.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu dedico este livro aos meus pais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicate this book to my parents.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of "dedicar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dedicou o livro ao pai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dedicated the book to her father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cortei o dedo a cozinhar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut my finger while cooking.

definitions.note: Plural of "dedo"; in Portuguese it can refer to both fingers and toes (often clarified with "dedos da mão" vs. "dedos do pé").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela machucou os dedos quando fechou a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hurt her fingers when she closed the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pelo que ele disse, posso deduzir que vai chover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From what he said, I can deduce that it's going to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deem bons conselhos aos filhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They give good advice to their children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este produto tem um defeito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product has a defect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O produto tem alguns defeitos, mas ainda funciona bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The product has some defects, but it still works well.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (they/you all) of “defender”; often used after expressions like “É importante que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que eles defendam os seus direitos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they defend their rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela defende o irmão na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She defends her brother at school.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "defender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está defendendo a irmã no tribunal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is defending his sister in court.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou defender os meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to defend my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele defendeu o amigo na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He defended his friend in the meeting.

definitions.note: Informal/conversational shortened form of the infinitive “defender,” used before object pronouns (e.g., “defendê-lo” = “defend him/it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou defendê-lo no debate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to defend him in the debate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A defesa do time foi muito boa no segundo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's defense was very good in the second half.

definitions.note: Often used for defending an idea, a person, or a position (including in court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez uma defesa forte do seu ponto de vista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a strong defense of his point of view.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio tem uma rampa para pessoas com deficiência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building has a ramp for people with disabilities.

definitions.note: Often used for a lack of something (e.g., nutrients, resources).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A deficiência de ferro pode causar cansaço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An iron deficiency can cause tiredness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prazo já está definido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deadline is already set.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a body with visible muscle definition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está bem definido depois de meses de treino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s really well-defined after months of training.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta é a resposta definitiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the definitive answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu definitivamente quero ir ao cinema hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I definitely want to go to the movies today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a definição desta palavra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the definition of this word?

definitions.note: Plural of "degrau".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Subi os degraus devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went up the steps slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dei um presente para ela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave her a present.

definitions.note: Can mean either “(he/she/it) lies down” (reflexive: deitar-se) or “(he/she/it) puts (something) down,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deita no sofá depois do trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lies down on the couch after work.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está deitada no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lying down on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone/something in a horizontal position (e.g., on a bed or on the ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está deitado no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is lying down on the couch.

definitions.native: to lie down, to lay down
definitions.note: Often used reflexively as “deitar-se” = “to lie down / go to bed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deitar mais cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to lie down earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (especially with “se”: “deite-se” = “lie down”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deite-se, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lie down, please.

definitions.native: I lay down, I put down
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito) of "deitar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou cansado, então deitei no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm tired, so I lay down on the couch.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular of “deitar” (he/she/it/you-formal lay down / put down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deitou no sofá e dormiu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lay down on the couch and fell asleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela cortou uma deixa do cabelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cut a lock of hair.

definitions.note: Usually means “lets/allows” (3rd person singular, present). It can also be used as an informal command meaning “leave it / stop it,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não deixa eu sair à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She doesn't let me go out at night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "deixar"; often used with "ser/estar" to form the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bolsa foi deixada no ônibus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bag was left on the bus.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves foram deixadas na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were left on the table.

definitions.note: Past participle of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro foi deixado na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was left on the table.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vós) command form; mostly seen in older, literary, or religious Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixai as crianças brincarem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) form of “deixar”; it can mean to leave something/someone somewhere or to allow/let something happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixam as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: From deixar; it can mean physically leaving something/someone or allowing/letting something happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixamos as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “deixar”; often used like “leaving” or “letting” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou deixando as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to let/allow” (e.g., deixar alguém fazer algo = to let someone do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode deixar a mala aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave the suitcase here.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they left.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram a cidade ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the city last night.

definitions.note: Often used with an object meaning “left something somewhere” or “let/allowed.” Simple past, 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixarei as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixarei você entrar se estiver com o ingresso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will let you in if you have the ticket.

definitions.note: This form is commonly used as (1) the future subjunctive (“if/when they leave/let”) or (2) the personal infinitive (“for them to leave/let”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se deixarem a porta aberta, o gato foge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they leave the door open, the cat runs away.

definitions.native: we will leave, we will let
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós deixaremos as malas aqui e voltaremos mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will leave the suitcases here and come back later.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “deixar” (often used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu deixaria as chaves na mesa, se você quiser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would leave the keys on the table, if you want.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixará as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) future tense of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixarão as malas no hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will leave the suitcases at the hotel.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu). Informal “you” in many regions; in Brazil it’s mostly used in some dialects and in Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu deixas a porta aberta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you leave the door open?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used after "se" (if) to express a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu deixasse a porta aberta, o gato fugia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I left the door open, the cat would run away.

definitions.native: you left, you let, you allowed
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), informal singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixaste a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the door open.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/habitual action in the past) of “deixar” (“to leave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deixava o carro na garagem todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the car in the garage every day.

definitions.note: Often used in polite requests/commands (to você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixe-me explicar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me explain.

definitions.note: Often used in polite requests/commands (to você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixe as chaves na mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the keys on the table, please.

definitions.native: I left, I let, I allowed
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixei o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the book on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixem as crianças brincar no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play in the park.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixem o carro aqui e venham comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the car here and come with me.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also the informal imperative) of “deixar” (used with “tu”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que não deixes a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't leave the door open.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") present tense of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu deixo o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the book on the table.

definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você) of “deixar”; can mean either leaving something somewhere or allowing something to happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixou o celular em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She left her cell phone at home.

definitions.note: Colloquial shortened form of “deixar”, common in informal speech and lyrics (especially in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deixá pra depois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll leave it for later.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "ela".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is hers.

definitions.note: Contraction of “de” + “ela”; used to show possession or relation (e.g., “the book is hers”, “a friend of hers”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro é dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is hers.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "elas"; refers to a group of females (or mixed group treated as feminine in context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A casa delas fica perto daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their house is close to here.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A delatora entregou os nomes à polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The informant gave the names to the police.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "ele"; often used after a noun to show possession (like "his").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro dele é vermelho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His car is red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou à delegacia para registrar a ocorrência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the police station to file the report.

definitions.note: Used for a masculine or mixed group (or when the possessed noun is masculine). For an all-female group, use "delas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este carro é deles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car is theirs.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "eles" (masculine/mixed plural); contrasts with "delas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro deles está na garagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their car is in the garage.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese, often used for deleting files, messages, or content (from English “delete”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode deletar essa mensagem, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you delete this message, please?

definitions.note: Informal; common in Brazilian Portuguese (from English “delete”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deletou a mensagem por engano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deleted the message by mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele quebrou o vaso deliberadamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the vase deliberately.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela embrulhou o presente com cuidado.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hospital is full of emergencies today.

definitions.note: Often used for feeling emotionally touched (e.g., by news or a moment), not just enthusiastic excitement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi um jogo emocionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exciting game.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt a great emotion when I saw my friends again.

definitions.note: Plural form of "emoção".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Emotions can change quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O final do filme foi empolgante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie was exciting.

definitions.note: Often used for a business project or investment; can also refer to a real-estate development.

definitions.note: Feminine form; can refer to a female employee in general (depending on context).

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) present tense of "emprestar".

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pen is borrowed.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As cadeiras foram emprestadas pela vizinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chairs were borrowed from the neighbor.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like "dinheiro emprestado" (borrowed money) or "livro emprestado" (a borrowed/lent book), depending on perspective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é emprestado, tenho de o devolver amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is borrowed; I have to return it tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os livros estão emprestados até sexta-feira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are loaned out until Friday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me emprestar o seu livro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me your book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou me encarando durante a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept staring at me during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encheram o copo de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They filled the glass with water.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “encher” (to fill).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele encheu a garrafa de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He filled the bottle with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei uma enciclopédia para estudar em casa.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “encontrar” (used with ele/ela/você).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds the keys in her bag.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He meets his friends at the café.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "encontrar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi/estava encontrada").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wallet was found near the bench.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (often used as a past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves foram encontradas no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were found on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O anel foi encontrado no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ring was found in the garden.

definitions.note: past participle (plural masculine) of “encontrar”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They find the keys in the drawer.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially Brazilian) spoken form of “encontramos” (final -s is dropped in speech and sometimes written that way).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met at the movie theater entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found the keys in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my keys.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person plural (they/you all).

definitions.note: Future subjunctive form, used after certain conjunctions (e.g., quando, se) to talk about a future possibility/condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles encontrarem a chave, abrem a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they find the key, they open the door.

definitions.native: we will find, we will meet
definitions.note: Future tense ("we" form). Can mean finding something or meeting someone, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã encontraremos um bom lugar para almoçar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will find a good place to have lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontraria você na estação, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would meet you at the station, but I’m sick.

definitions.native: (for us) to meet, (for us) to find
definitions.note: Personal infinitive (infinitivo pessoal), used with an explicit subject like “nós” (“we”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor encontrarmos um lugar tranquilo para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to find a quiet place to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você encontrará a chave na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the key in the drawer.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future tense of “encontrar”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will find a good restaurant near the hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found the keys, I would let you know.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraste as chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse bolo está gostoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cake is tasty.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person's physical attractiveness; can sound flirtatious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito gostoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very good-looking.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gostar": “(he/she/you formal) liked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gostou do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She liked the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caiu uma gota de água na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A drop of water fell on the table.

definitions.note: Plural of "gota".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cairam algumas gotas de chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A few drops of rain fell.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a roof/ceiling leak where water drips inside.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem uma goteira no teto da cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a leak in the kitchen ceiling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela governa o país com firmeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She governs the country firmly.

definitions.note: Used for the head of a state/province, or for the head of certain institutions (e.g., a central bank).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O governador anunciou novas medidas para a segurança pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The governor announced new measures for public safety.

definitions.note: Often refers to a woman hired to manage a household; depending on context it can also mean a governess (a private tutor/nanny for children).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A governanta organiza a casa e supervisiona os empregados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The housekeeper organizes the house and supervises the employees.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a person employed to manage a household (domestic staff, cleaning, organization).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A governante organizou os quartos antes da chegada dos hóspedes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The housekeeper organized the rooms before the guests arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O governo anunciou novas medidas econômicas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government announced new economic measures.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of "governar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela governou o país por quatro anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She governed the country for four years.

definitions.note: Often used as an affectionate way to refer to someone (especially a child). It can also be used ironically to mean someone is being a “smart-aleck,” depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vem cá, gracinha, deixa eu te ajudar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, cutie, let me help you.

definitions.note: Often refers to metal bars on windows/doors (like security bars). Not related to English "grades" (school marks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As grades da janela estão enferrujadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window bars are rusty.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts, especially for military or hierarchical ranks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele alcançou o grado de sargento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reached the rank of sergeant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As coisas melhoraram gradualmente ao longo do ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Things improved gradually over the year.

definitions.note: Often refers to receiving an academic degree or the degree itself (especially in higher education).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai terminar a graduação em engenharia este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to finish her engineering degree this year.

definitions.note: Feminine when it means “grass” (a grama).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A grama do jardim está bem verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grass in the garden is very green.

definitions.note: Masculine when it means the unit of weight (o grama); very common in the plural (gramas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de duzentas gramas de queijo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two hundred grams of cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças brincam no gramado do parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children play on the park lawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me emprestar o grampeador?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me the stapler?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou a estudar gramática portuguesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying Portuguese grammar.

definitions.note: Informal (Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou sem grana este mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m out of money this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No mercado, comprei duas granadas bem maduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the market, I bought two very ripe pomegranates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os soldados jogaram granadas durante o treinamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers threw grenades during training.

definitions.note: Often means “big/large” (usually after the noun). Before a noun, it can mean “great” in the sense of important/admired (e.g., “um grande amigo” = “a great friend”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A casa é grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is big.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As casas são grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses are big.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele mostrou grandeza ao admitir que estava errado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed greatness by admitting he was wrong.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sou muito grata pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sinto muita gratidão por tudo o que você fez por mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of gratitude for everything you did for me.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to say who/what you’re grateful for (e.g., "grato a você").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sou muito grato pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Somos muito gratos pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada do museu é gratuita, então você pode entrar gratuitamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum entry is free, so you can go in for free.

definitions.note: Often used for services, events, or items that cost no money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada é gratuita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free.

definitions.note: Commonly used for temperature (graus Celsius/Fahrenheit) and for levels or intensity (e.g., a high degree of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje está a 30 graus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s 30 degrees.

definitions.note: Often used for levels in school or hierarchy (e.g., primeiro grau).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está no primeiro grau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in first grade.

definitions.note: Plural of "grau". Commonly used for temperature (°C/°F) and angles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje faz 30 graus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s 30 degrees.

definitions.note: Often refers to an audio/voice recorder or recording device.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um gravador para gravar as aulas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a recorder to record the classes.

definitions.note: Often used for recording audio/video; depending on context it can also mean “filming.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou gravando um vídeo para a aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m recording a video for class.

definitions.note: Often used for recording audio or video.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou gravar um vídeo para a aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to record a video for class.

definitions.note: Used for marking or carving words/images onto a surface (metal, wood, stone, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles vão gravar o nome dela no anel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to engrave her name on the ring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele colocou uma gravata azul para a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put on a blue tie for the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem várias gravatas no armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has several ties in the closet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gravação da aula ficou muito clara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The recording of the class was very clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente foi grave, mas ninguém morreu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident was serious, but nobody died.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou gravemente ferido no acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was seriously injured in the accident.

definitions.note: Adjective in the plural form (masculine or feminine, depending on the noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: São problemas graves, mas vamos resolvê-los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are serious problems, but we’re going to solve them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gravidade mantém a Terra em órbita ao redor do Sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gravity keeps the Earth in orbit around the Sun.

definitions.note: Often used for the seriousness of a situation, problem, or offense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não entendeu a gravidade do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t understand the seriousness of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está no terceiro mês de gravidez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in the third month of pregnancy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gravou a aula no celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She recorded the class on her phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O joalheiro gravou o nome dela no anel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jeweler engraved her name on the ring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele respondeu com graça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replied with grace.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression "fazer graça" (to joke around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez uma graça para nos fazer rir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a joke to make us laugh.

definitions.note: Common in religious contexts (e.g., "pela graça de Deus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi pela graça de Deus que tudo deu certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was by God's grace that everything worked out.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “graças a …” meaning “thanks to …” (e.g., “Graças a Deus” = “Thank God”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Graças a você, conseguimos terminar o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks to you, we managed to finish the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dançava com graças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She danced with grace.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é grega e mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Greek and lives in Lisbon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está estudando literatura grega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is studying Greek literature.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a Greek person; it can also refer to the Greek language depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é grego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Greek.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo grego na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Greek at the university.

definitions.note: plural masculine (refers to more than one male person or a mixed group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os turistas gregos chegaram ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greek tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural of "grego" (a Greek person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os gregos têm uma história muito antiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greeks have a very ancient history.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “(he/she/it) grilled.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele grelhou o frango no carvão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grilled the chicken over charcoal.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a work stoppage/protest by workers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os professores fizeram greve por melhores salários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers went on strike for better pay.

definitions.note: Common in Brazil/Latin America to refer to a foreigner (often someone from the U.S. or Europe). Depending on context/tone it can be neutral or mildly pejorative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é gringo, mas fala português muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a foreigner, but he speaks Portuguese very well.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the verb "estar" (e.g., "estou gripado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou gripado e vou ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I'm going to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou com gripe e vou ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I’m going to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu avô está com o cabelo bem grisalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather’s hair is very gray.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “gritar” (also used in commands like “Shout!” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela grita quando está com medo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shouts when she’s scared.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “gritar” (used like “shouting/yelling” or “while shouting/yelling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele entrou na sala gritando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walked into the room shouting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não precisa gritar comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don't need to shout at me.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) for “they” (and also “you all” in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles gritaram quando viram o acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They shouted when they saw the accident.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gritava com o irmão todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to shout at his brother every day.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for negative commands with você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não grite comigo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't shout at me, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gritar" for the first person singular (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gritei porque estava com medo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted because I was scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ouvi um grito na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a shout in the street.

definitions.note: Plural of “grito”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ouvimos gritos na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard shouts in the street.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gritar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gritou com o irmão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted at his brother.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone feeling unwell, dizzy, or slow (for example, from lack of sleep, alcohol, or medication).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do remédio, fiquei grogue o resto do dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the medicine, I felt groggy for the rest of the day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "grosso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A corda é muito grossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rope is very thick.

definitions.note: Often means “thick” (size/width). It does not usually mean English “gross” (= disgusting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As cordas são grossas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ropes are thick.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As piadas dele eram grosseiras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His jokes were rude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi grosseiro com a garçonete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was rude to the waitress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma grosseria o que ele disse na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What he said in the meeting was rude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpe a grosseria, eu não quis ofender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the rude remark; I didn’t mean to offend.

definitions.note: Often refers to physical size or thickness; for people it can mean “fat” (can sound rude depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou um livro grosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a thick book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O nosso grupo vai se encontrar às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our group is going to meet at seven.

definitions.note: Plural of "grupo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os grupos de estudantes apresentaram seus projetos hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The groups of students presented their projects today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles entraram na gruta para se abrigar da chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went into the cave to shelter from the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este gráfico mostra as vendas do último mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chart shows last month's sales.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun: "entrada grátis" = "free entry".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada é grátis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry is free.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with women).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está grávida de três meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is three months pregnant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pão tem grãos de trigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread has wheat grains.

definitions.note: Plural of "grão"; often used for cereal grains or coffee beans depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei grãos de café para fazer um café mais fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought coffee beans to make fresher coffee.

definitions.note: Often used for a person whose job is to protect or watch over a place (e.g., a security guard). It can be used with either article: o guarda / a guarda.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guarda está na entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guard is at the entrance of the building.

definitions.note: From the verb "guardar"; often used for keeping/storing something in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guarda as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps the keys in her bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me passar um guardanapo, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me a napkin, please?

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while keeping/storing" or "(is) keeping/storing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou guardando os documentos na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m keeping the documents in the drawer.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while watching over" or "(is) looking after").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está guardando as crianças enquanto eu trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s looking after the kids while I work.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something away in a safe place or saving it for later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou guardar estas fotos numa caixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to keep these photos in a box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cão vai guardar a casa à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog will guard the house at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guardas vigiam a entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guards watch the entrance to the building.

definitions.note: Usually a formal command (“you” singular) or the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “é importante que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarde este recibo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep this receipt.

definitions.native: I kept, I saved, I put away
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardei o dinheiro na carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the money away in my wallet.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) or affirmative imperative (vocês) of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardem os documentos em um lugar seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the documents in a safe place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guardião do museu fechou as portas às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum’s guardian closed the doors at six.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guardou as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept the keys in her purse.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele guardou os brinquedos depois de brincar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put away the toys after playing.

definitions.note: Common colloquial spoken form of “guardar” (to keep/store), especially in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pode guardá isso pra mim?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you keep this for me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem à noite, vimos um guaxinim perto do lixo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, we saw a raccoon near the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guerra acabou depois de muitos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war ended after many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As guerras mudaram a história do país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wars changed the country’s history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guerreiro voltou para casa depois da batalha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warrior returned home after the battle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guerreiros voltaram para a aldeia depois da batalha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warriors returned to the village after the battle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guia explicou a história da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide explained the history of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um guia de viagem para o Porto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a travel guidebook for Porto.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor vai guiar os alunos durante a visita ao museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is going to guide the students during the visit to the museum.

definitions.note: Common in contexts like driving a car (especially in European Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sabe guiar muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She knows how to drive very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guindaste levantou a viga de aço com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crane lifted the steel beam carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guiar” for ele/ela/você.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guiou o grupo até a entrada do museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guided the group to the museum entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu toco guitarra todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play guitar every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guitarrista toca muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitarist plays very well.

definitions.note: Usually masculine: o gás.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gás acabou e precisamos comprar outro botijão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas ran out and we need to buy another gas cylinder.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma irmã gêmea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a twin sister.

definitions.note: Feminine plural; refers to twin girls or women.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As gêmeas estudam na mesma escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twin girls study at the same school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmão é gêmeo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a twin.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os gêmeos têm o mesmo aniversário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twins have the same birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na ficha, você precisa indicar seu gênero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, you need to indicate your gender.

definitions.note: Common for categories like music, movies, and books.
