definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pain became unbearable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A intolerância pode causar conflitos desnecessários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Intolerance can cause unnecessary conflicts.

definitions.note: Often used for food poisoning (e.g., “intoxicação alimentar”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele teve intoxicação depois de comer frutos do mar estragados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had food poisoning after eating spoiled seafood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei intrigado com o que ele disse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was intrigued by what he said.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gosta de se intrometer na conversa dos outros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to meddle in other people's conversations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é mais introvertido do que o irmão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more introverted than his brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O segurança tirou o intruso do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The security guard removed the intruder from the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tive a intuição de que algo ia dar errado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the intuition that something was going to go wrong.

definitions.note: Can refer to someone who translates spoken language or to a performer who interprets music/acting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha como intérprete em conferências internacionais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works as an interpreter at international conferences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A inundação deixou muitas ruas debaixo d’água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flood left many streets underwater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As inundações destruíram várias casas na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floods destroyed several houses in the city.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cidade foi invadida durante a noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was invaded during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O exército decidiu invadir o país vizinho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army decided to invade the neighboring country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os soldados invadiram a cidade ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers invaded the city at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O exército invadiu a cidade ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army invaded the city at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A invasão começou ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The invasion began at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu inveja do sucesso dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt envy of her success.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense ("I envy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu invejo a sua coragem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy your courage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este time parece invencível nesta temporada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team seems invincible this season.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa história foi inventada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That story was made up.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to make something up” (a story, excuse, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele inventou uma desculpa para faltar ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made up an excuse to miss work.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (eu) or imperative (você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu não invente desculpas de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I don't invent excuses again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu inventei uma desculpa para não sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made up an excuse not to go out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O inventor criou um novo tipo de bateria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inventor created a new type of battery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela inventou uma desculpa para faltar à aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She made up an excuse to miss class.

definitions.note: Common colloquial spelling/pronunciation of the infinitive "inventar" in some Brazilian Portuguese accents (dropping the final -r).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não vai inventá desculpa agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t go making up an excuse now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa invenção mudou a forma como as pessoas se comunicam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That invention changed the way people communicate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No inverno, faz frio aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the winter, it’s cold here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os investidores estão otimistas com o mercado este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investors are optimistic about the market this year.

definitions.note: Plural form of "investigador".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os investigadores chegaram cedo para analisar as provas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigators arrived early to analyze the evidence.

definitions.note: Gerund (ongoing action), often used with “estar” to mean “to be investigating.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia está investigando o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia vai investigar o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to investigate the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia abriu uma investigação sobre o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police opened an investigation into the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia investigou o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police investigated the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este investimento vai trazer bons resultados no futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This investment will bring good results in the future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer investir em ações.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to invest in stocks.

definitions.note: Common in European Portuguese; in Brazilian Portuguese, "vestir" is more common for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou investir o casaco porque está frio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to put on my coat because it's cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele investiu em ações no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invested in stocks last year.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À noite, as estrelas ficam quase invisíveis por causa das luzes da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, the stars become almost invisible because of the city lights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gás é invisível, mas é perigoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas is invisible, but it’s dangerous.

definitions.note: Almost always used in the expression “ao invés de …” (also commonly “em vez de …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ao invés de estudar, ele ficou vendo TV.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of studying, he kept watching TV.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No início do filme, ele está em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the beginning of the movie, he is at home.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form, used before a feminine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem inúmeras ideias para o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has countless ideas for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há inúmeros motivos para aprender português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are countless reasons to learn Portuguese.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas ferramentas são inúteis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those tools are useless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este computador velho é inútil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This old computer is useless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faço ioga duas vezes por semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do yoga twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu como iogurte no café da manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat yogurt for breakfast.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary to form the near future: ir + infinitive (e.g., vou + infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou ir visitar meus avós amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to visit my grandparents tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + place (e.g., ir ao mercado = go to the market).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso ir agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A ira dele foi diminuindo com o tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger gradually decreased over time.

definitions.note: More formal/literary than common everyday options like "bravo" or "zangado".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou irado com a decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got furious about the decision.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular (eu) simple future of ir.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã irei ao médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go to the doctor.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã irei ao mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go to the market.

definitions.note: Future subjunctive of "ir" (used after certain conjunctions like "quando", "se", "antes que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eles irem ao mercado, vão comprar frutas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they go to the market, they’re going to buy fruit.

definitions.note: 1st person plural ("we") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã iremos ao mercado cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will go to the market early.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã iremos ao cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will go to the movies.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the verb/auxiliary “ir” (often used to talk about something that would happen, or a future-in-the-past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu iria com você, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go with you, but I’m sick.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "ir" (to go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu iria com você, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go with you, but I'm sick.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary with an infinitive (e.g., "iriam fazer" = "would do / were going to do").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles iriam comprar um carro, mas desistiram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were going to buy a car, but they changed their minds.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for women or feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha professora é irlandesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Irish.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os músicos irlandeses tocaram no festival ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Irish musicians played at the festival yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é irlandês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Irish.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive of "ir" used with "nós" (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor irmos agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmã mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Can mean a biological brother or be used informally to refer to a close male friend (like “bro”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmão mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Plural of “irmão”. Can also refer to siblings (brothers and sisters) in some contexts, but “irmãos” literally means “brothers”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dois irmãos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “irmão”; can express small size or affection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmãozinho ainda está na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My little brother is still at school.

definitions.note: plural feminine form of “irmã”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Minhas irmãs moram em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters live in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "irmã"; often expresses affection (like “sis” or “little sis”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmãzinha adora desenhar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My little sister loves to draw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma decisão irracional.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an irrational decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O horário do ônibus é irregular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus schedule is irregular.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse detalhe é irrelevante para a nossa decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That detail is irrelevant to our decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse bolo é irresistível.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cake is irresistible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi irresponsável da sua parte dirigir depois de beber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was irresponsible of you to drive after drinking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho me irrita muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise irritates me a lot.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou irritada com o atraso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got irritated about the delay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está irritado com o trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is irritated about the traffic.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão irritados com o barulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are irritated by the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses comentários irritam muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments irritate (annoy) a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho é muito irritante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is very annoying.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "irritar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O barulho do trânsito irritou o vizinho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic noise irritated the neighbor.

definitions.note: Future tense form of "ir". As an auxiliary, it introduces an infinitive (e.g., "irá fazer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele irá estudar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will study tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) simple future of “ir” (to go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela irá ao médico amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will go to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense; often sounds formal in Brazil (where “você vai” is more common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã, irás ao médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, you will go to the doctor.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they) of the verb/auxiliary “ir” in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles irão viajar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will travel tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (eles/elas/vocês) future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles irão ao mercado amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will go to the market tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "ir"; often used to talk about what someone would do in a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se tivéssemos tempo, iríamos ao cinema hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had time, we would go to the movies today.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a sarcastic or mocking tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi irônico ele criticar a bagunça depois de deixar tudo fora do lugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was ironic for him to criticize the mess after leaving everything out of place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pescador colocou a isca no anzol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman put the bait on the hook.

definitions.note: Refers to political Islam (a political ideology/movement), not the religion Islam in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O islamismo é um tema debatido em muitos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Islamism is a topic debated in many countries.

definitions.note: Refers to a person from Iceland; the feminine form is “islandesa”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é islandês e mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Icelandic and lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Can also refer to the Icelandic language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou a aprender islandês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Icelandic.

definitions.note: Name of the religion; often capitalized in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O islã é praticado em muitos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Islam is practiced in many countries.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A casa fica isolada no meio do campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is isolated in the middle of the countryside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele mora em um lugar isolado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in an isolated place.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something or someone is apart from others (not connected or included).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse é um caso isolado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an isolated case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O isolamento ajudou a reduzir a transmissão do vírus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The isolation helped reduce the transmission of the virus.

definitions.note: Common Brazilian Portuguese term for expanded polystyrene foam (EPS).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A caixa de isopor mantém as bebidas geladas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Styrofoam cooler keeps the drinks cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem um isqueiro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a lighter?

definitions.note: Neutral demonstrative (not masculine/feminine); often refers to something already mentioned or something closer to the listener than to the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que é isso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is that?

definitions.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun used to refer to a thing/idea (not usually a person), often something already mentioned or near the listener.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso é muito importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is very important.

definitions.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun (used for things/ideas, not people), often for something close to the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isto é muito importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is very important.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to refer to a woman)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Italian.

definitions.note: Usually describes something from Italy; when referring to a person, it can mean “Italian (man)” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fala italiano muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks Italian very well.

definitions.note: Can also refer to an Italian person; this entry is for the language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou a aprender italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Italian.

definitions.note: plural masculine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os turistas italianos chegaram ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Italian tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos italianos nesta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Italians in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O primeiro item da lista é o mais importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first item on the list is the most important.

definitions.note: Plural of "item".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A lista tem três itens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The list has three items.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos um jacaré no rio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw an alligator in the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu nunca vou esquecer isso — jamais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll never forget that — ever.

definitions.note: Often used in negative sentences and questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você já viajou para a Europa alguma vez? Não, jamais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you ever traveled to Europe? No, never.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu aniversário é em janeiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abre a janela, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Open the window, please.

definitions.note: plural of "janela"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As janelas estão abertas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows are open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A janta está pronta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dinner is ready.

definitions.note: Present tense form of the verb “jantar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela janta às oito da noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She eats dinner at eight o'clock at night.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “jantar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles jantam às oito da noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have dinner at eight at night.

definitions.native: we had dinner, we ate dinner
definitions.note: Can mean either simple past (“we had dinner”) or present (“we have dinner”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem jantamos cedo em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we had dinner early at home.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "jantar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão jantando agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are having dinner now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos preparar o jantar juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s prepare dinner together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gente vai jantar às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to have dinner at eight.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (eles/elas/vocês) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles jantaram cedo ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had dinner early yesterday.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for polite/negative commands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você jante cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you have dinner early today.

definitions.native: I had dinner, I ate dinner
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of “jantar” (to have dinner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem eu jantei em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had dinner at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele jantou cedo ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had dinner early yesterday.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns, or about a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A culinária japonesa é muito popular aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Japanese cuisine is very popular here.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As estudantes japonesas são muito simpáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Japanese (female) students are very nice.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form (used for a group of men or a mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os turistas japoneses chegaram hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Japanese tourists arrived today.

definitions.note: Plural form; refers to Japanese people (not the language).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os japoneses vivem no Japão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Japanese people live in Japan.

definitions.note: Can describe something/someone from Japan; as an adjective it agrees with the noun (japonesa, japoneses, japonesas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de comida japonesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Japanese food.

definitions.note: As a noun, it usually refers to a Japanese person; it can also be used as an adjective meaning “Japanese.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O japonês mora aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Japanese man lives here.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb “falar” (to speak).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falo japonês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Japanese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou uma jaqueta nova para o inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a new jacket for the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos um jardim pequeno atrás da casa.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take the children to school every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take the kids to school every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They get up early every day.

definitions.native: we get up, we stand up, we lift, we raise

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We get up early every day.

definitions.native: I get up, I stand up, I lift

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get up early every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they took/carried” (also used for “you all” in Brazil).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take my son to school every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cows are in the pasture.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shepherd took the sheep to the field.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an animal’s paw/leg (especially a four-legged animal).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro sujou as patas na lama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog got its paws dirty in the mud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa registrou uma patente para a nova tecnologia.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de patinar no parque aos domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to skate in the park on Sundays.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car started to skid on the wet road.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She put on her skates and went skating in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O patrão está no escritório agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is in the office now.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “pitiful” or “lame” (a negative judgment), not “emotionally moving.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought it was pathetic that he lied over something so small.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up a stick from the ground to lean on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos fazer uma pausa de cinco minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take a five-minute break.

definitions.note: Plural of "pauzinho"; can refer to small sticks like toothpicks or chopsticks depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegue dois pauzinhos para prender o papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take two little sticks to hold the paper in place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos viver em paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to live in peace.

definitions.note: Plural of "paz"; often used in fixed expressions like "em paz" (at peace) or "fazer as pazes" (make up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de tanta discussão, eles finalmente fizeram as pazes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After so much arguing, they finally made up.

definitions.note: The accent matters: “país” means “country,” while “pais” (no accent) means “parents.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Portugal is a small country, but very beautiful.

definitions.note: Plural of "país".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela já visitou muitos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has already visited many countries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mentir é um pecado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lying is a sin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele confessou os pecados ao padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed his sins to the priest.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "pedaço"; often used to sound affectionate or to emphasize smallness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você quer um pedacinho de bolo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a small piece of cake?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero um pedaço de bolo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a piece of cake, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "pedaço".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cortei o bolo em pedaços.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the cake into pieces.

definitions.note: Present tense (ele/ela/você) of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pede ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks the teacher for help.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all) form of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pedem ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ask the teacher for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pedestres devem atravessar na faixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pedestrians should cross at the crosswalk.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of “pedir” for “eu”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedi um café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked for a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Commonly used for ordering food or making a formal request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiz um pedido no restaurante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I placed an order at the restaurant.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório foi pedido ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report was requested yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pedidos chegaram hoje de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The orders arrived this morning.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós) of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós pedimos ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ask the teacher for help.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "pedir" (used like “asking/requesting”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pedindo ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am asking the teacher for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pedir um café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to ask for a coffee, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pediu a sobremesa depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She ordered dessert after dinner.

definitions.note: Past tense (simple past) form meaning “they asked for / they requested.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pediram ajuda depois do acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked for help after the accident.

definitions.native: I will ask (for), I will request
definitions.note: 1st-person singular future tense of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedirei ajuda se eu precisar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will ask for help if I need it.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "pedir" (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pediria uma pizza, mas não estou com fome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would ask for a pizza, but I'm not hungry.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form, used in hypothetical or dependent clauses (often with “se”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu pedisse ajuda, você viria?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I asked for help, would you come?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pediu um café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked for a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pegou uma pedra do chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up a stone from the ground.

definitions.note: Plural of "pedra".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitas pedras no caminho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many stones on the path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O caminho estava coberto de pedregulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path was covered with gravel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pega construiu o ninho naquela árvore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magpie built the nest in that tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pega o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As pegadas na areia mostram que alguém passou por aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The footprints in the sand show that someone passed by here.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is stuck/glued to something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O adesivo ficou pegado no vidro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sticker got stuck on the glass.

definitions.note: Common with illnesses or problems (e.g., “pegar uma gripe” = to catch the flu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está pegado com uma gripe forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s down with a bad flu.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “pegar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegam o ônibus às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take the bus at seven.

definitions.native: we got, we caught, we took
definitions.note: Often used meaning “we got/caught” (e.g., a bus, a cold) or “we took/grabbed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegamos o ônibus às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We caught the bus at seven.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to form the ongoing action (progressive), like "estou pegando" = "I am getting/taking".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pegando o ônibus agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m catching the bus now.

definitions.native: to take, to grab, to pick up
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode pegar este livro para mim?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pick up this book for me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pegar o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to catch the bus at eight.

definitions.native: to catch (an illness), to get (a cold)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pegou uma gripe forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He caught a bad flu.

definitions.native: they took, they grabbed, they picked up
definitions.note: Past (completed action): third-person plural of "pegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegaram o ônibus cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus early.

definitions.note: Often used for catching something (like a ball) or catching an illness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegaram a bola no ar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They caught the ball in the air.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., with “se” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu pegasse o ônibus mais cedo, chegaria a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I caught the bus earlier, I would arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pego o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural). Often used with "ser" to mean "to be caught".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles foram pegos pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were caught by the police.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você form) of "pegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pegou o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up the book from the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a (você) command (“Take/Grab ...”). It can also be the present subjunctive form of pegar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegue o livro, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the book, please.

definitions.native: I got, I took, I caught
definitions.note: Past tense (eu) of "pegar"; often used for getting/taking something, or catching something (like a bus or a cold).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peguei o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or affirmative command) form of "pegar" for "vocês".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peguem os livros e venham comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the books and come with me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to grab the coat because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu uma dor no peito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a pain in his chest.

definitions.note: Plural of "peito". In everyday speech it can mean either the chest (body part) or breasts, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu uma dor nos peitos ao respirar fundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a pain in his chest when taking a deep breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de comer peixe no jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to eat fish for dinner.

definitions.note: Plural of "peixe".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos peixes no aquário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many fish in the aquarium.

definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "a" (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked along the beach at sunset.

definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "a" (feminine singular). Often used to show who did something (agent) or what something is exchanged for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro foi escrito pela Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book was written by Ana.

definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "a" (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is bald.

definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "as" (feminine plural "the").

definitions.native: through the, by the, along the
definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "as" (feminine plural "the").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caminhamos pelas ruas do centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked through the streets downtown.

definitions.note: Contraction of “por” + “as” (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passamos pelas ruas estreitas do centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went through the narrow streets downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His skin is very sensitive to the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Animals' skins vary a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat has soft fur.

definitions.note: Contraction of "por" + "o" ("the", masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passei pelo parque depois do trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I walked through the park after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passei pelos parques ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went through the parks yesterday.

definitions.note: Usually used in military contexts; also used figuratively for an organized group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pelotão avançou ao amanhecer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um ursinho de pelúcia para o meu sobrinho.

definitions.native: what a pity, what a shame

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a pity! I wanted to go with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrei uma pena no chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a feather on the ground.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “Que pena!” (“What a pity!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que pena que você não pode vir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a pity you can’t come.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pássaro perdeu algumas penas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird lost some feathers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As penas para esse crime são severas.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant is hanging on the balcony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O casaco está pendurado atrás da porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coat is hanging behind the door.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is in debt on his credit card.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Penduramos o quadro na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hung the picture on the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pendurar o casaco no armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to hang the coat up in the closet.

definitions.note: Informal in many contexts (e.g., “pendurar uma conversa” = to stall/drag out a conversation).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to postpone the meeting until next week.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form: used to tell someone to hang something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pendure o casaco no cabide, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hang the coat on the hanger, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pendurou o casaco no cabide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hung the coat on the hanger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegaram ao topo do penhasco ao pôr do sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They reached the top of the cliff at sunset.

definitions.note: Present tense (ele/ela/você).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thinks it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pensar"; often used like an adjective meaning "thought out" or "well planned."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso foi bem pensado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was well thought out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pensadores discutiram novas ideias na conferência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thinkers discussed new ideas at the conference.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all think).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pensam que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s going to rain today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse pensamento me deixou mais calmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That thought made me calmer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho muitos pensamentos hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many thoughts today.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensamos que isso é uma boa ideia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think that this is a good idea.

definitions.note: Gerund/present participle of "pensar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be thinking".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pensando no que você disse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m thinking about what you said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso pensar antes de responder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to think before answering.

definitions.note: Often used with “em” (pensar em) to mean planning or intending to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pensando em viajar no fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning to travel this weekend.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito): refers to “they thought” (or “you all thought” in European Portuguese).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the movie was very long.

definitions.note: Conditional form (often used for hypotheticals or polite/indirect statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pensaria duas vezes antes de aceitar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would think twice before accepting.

definitions.note: Usually means “you think” (2nd person singular, present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que pensas sobre este problema?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you think about this problem?

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu), simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensaste nisso ontem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you think about that yesterday?

definitions.note: Past imperfect of "pensar"; often means "was thinking" or "used to think," depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pensava que a loja abria às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought the store opened at eight.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (they thought / were thinking; also used for ‘you all’ in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pensavam que ia chover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought it was going to rain.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (formal “you”), or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I want you to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pense antes de falar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think before you speak.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "pensar" in the first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensei que você já tinha saído.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you had already left.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or imperative) form of "pensar" used with "vocês" (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero que vocês pensem nisso com calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you all to think about that calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Penso que ele tem razão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he's right.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “pensar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pensou na viagem o dia todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thought about the trip all day.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação contínua/habitual no passado).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thought the movie was going to be boring, but it was great.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a comb to fix my hair.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked your hairstyle.

definitions.note: Gerund ("-ing" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou penteando o meu cabelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am combing my hair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou pentear o cabelo antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to comb my hair before leaving.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “pentear” for ele/ela/você.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela penteou o cabelo antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She combed her hair before leaving.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need insurance for the car.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sure that they will arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela segurou a minha mão durante o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She held my hand during the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to hold it for you.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "saber" used with the meaning "to know" (facts, information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sei a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the answer.

definitions.note: From the verb “saber”; used for knowing facts or how to do something (not for knowing people/places).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sei a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela usou um sutiã que oferecia mais suporte aos seios.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tenho seis livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have six books.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum received six hundred visitors yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A seiva circula dentro do caule da planta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sap circulates inside the plant’s stem.

definitions.note: Often used after “que” (subjunctive) and to form the passive voice with a past participle.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that the report be sent today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "ser"; also used in the polite imperative (e.g., "Seja bem-vindo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você seja feliz aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you are happy here.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) of “ser”; often used after expressions of desire, doubt, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles sejam pontuais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they are punctual.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive of “ser”; often used to make suggestions or wishes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sejamos pacientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s be patient.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "ser" (used after expressions like "I hope that...", "it’s important that...", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que sejas feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you are happy.

definitions.note: Past participle of "selecionar"; often used like an adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The selected item appears in blue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os selecionados serão anunciados amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The selected people will be announced tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of "selecionar"; commonly used as an adjective or in passive/compound tenses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The selected students will receive an email tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A seleção de filmes deste ano está ótima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This year’s selection of movies is great.

definitions.note: Often used in sports, especially to refer to Brazil’s or another country’s national team (e.g., futebol).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Brazilian national team played very well yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tirei uma selfie na praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a selfie at the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de um selo para enviar esta carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a stamp to send this letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de dois selos para enviar estas cartas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two stamps to send these letters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A selva amazônica é muito rica em biodiversidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Amazon rainforest is very rich in biodiversity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos um cavalo selvagem na montanha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a wild horse in the mountains.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person’s behavior or an attack as very violent or cruel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi um ataque selvagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a savage attack.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os animais selvagens vivem na floresta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wild animals live in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural of the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os selvagens atacaram a aldeia ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The savages attacked the village at dawn.

definitions.note: Often sounds offensive in modern usage; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No livro antigo, ele descreve os moradores da ilha como selvagens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the old book, he describes the island’s residents as wild people.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun or an infinitive (e.g., "sem dinheiro", "sem saber").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m without money today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu trabalho cinco dias por semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work five days a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou à academia semanalmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym weekly.

definitions.note: plural of "semana"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will stay here for two weeks.

definitions.note: Present tense form of the verb “semear” (to sow/seed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele semeia as sementes na horta todos os anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sows the seeds in the vegetable garden every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles têm ideias semelhantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have similar ideas.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have similar ideas about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há uma grande semelhança entre as duas fotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big similarity between the two photos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plantei uma semente no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a seed in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plantei sementes de tomate no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted tomato seeds in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre tenho aulas de português duas vezes por semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I have Portuguese classes twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sempre tomo café de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always drink coffee in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O semáforo ficou vermelho e todos os carros pararam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic light turned red and all the cars stopped.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há semáforos em todas as esquinas nesta avenida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are traffic lights on every corner on this avenue.

definitions.note: An old-fashioned or nonstandard written abbreviation of “senhor”; today it’s most common in historical texts or informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sen, posso fazer uma pergunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, may I ask a question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O senador fez um discurso no parlamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senator gave a speech in parliament.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "ser" used as an auxiliary (often meaning "being" in English).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being honest, I don’t know the answer.

definitions.note: Gerund of "ser" (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sendo sincero, eu não gostei do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being honest, I didn’t like the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a senha do Wi‑Fi?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the Wi‑Fi password?

definitions.note: Common in Brazil for a number you take to wait your turn (e.g., at a bank, pharmacy, deli).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegue uma senha e espere ser chamado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a ticket number and wait to be called.

definitions.note: A polite/formal way to address an adult man; often used like a title (e.g., Sr.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com licença, senhor, pode me ajudar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, sir, can you help me?

definitions.note: Polite/formal way to address a man; often used with a last name (e.g., Senhor Silva).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senhor, pode me ajudar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, can you help me?

definitions.note: Polite form of address for an adult woman; also used before a last name (like “Mrs.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com licença, senhora, a senhora deixou sua bolsa aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, ma’am, you left your bag here.

definitions.note: Plural of "senhora"; also used as a polite way to address a group of women (e.g., in speeches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senhoras e senhores, bem-vindos ao evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the event.

definitions.note: Plural of “senhor”; used as a polite form of address for men.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senhores, por favor, entrem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gentlemen, please come in.

definitions.note: Can also refer to a group of men in a formal or respectful way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os senhores já decidiram?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you gentlemen decided already?

definitions.note: Traditional/polite form of address for an unmarried woman; nowadays it can sound old-fashioned or be avoided in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com licença, senhorita, você sabe onde fica o banheiro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, miss, do you know where the bathroom is?

definitions.note: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, it’s a common enthusiastic compliment meaning “awesome/amazing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O show foi sensacional!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The show was amazing!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deu uma resposta sensata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave a sensible answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tive uma sensação estranha quando entrei na sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a strange feeling when I walked into the room.

definitions.note: Loanword from Japanese; often used in martial arts contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sensei explicou o movimento devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explained the move slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso não faz senso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That doesn't make sense.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "bom senso" (good judgment/common sense).

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people are very sensitive to noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito sensível e chora com facilidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very sensitive and cries easily.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a command (imperative) or with “você/ele/ela” in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senta aqui, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit here, please.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está sentada na cadeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is seated in the chair.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças estão sentadas no chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sitting on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está sentado no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão sentados no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are seated on the couch.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech as a shortened form of “sentamos” (Brazilian Portuguese).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat down there and talked a bit.

definitions.note: Can mean present (we sit) or simple past (we sat), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do almoço, sentamos na sala para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch, we sat in the living room to talk.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: sentar-se = “to sit down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou sentar aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit here.

definitions.note: Third-person plural simple past (preterite): “they” (or “you all” in some regions) sat down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles sentaram perto da janela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sat down near the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ele sentasse aqui, seria mais fácil conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he sat here, it would be easier to talk.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite command with você (e.g., “Sente-se”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sente-se aqui, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit here, please.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "sentir"; can also mean "smells" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sente muita saudade da família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels a lot of longing for her family.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "sentar" for "eu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me sentei no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat down on the couch.

definitions.note: Affirmative command for vocês (you all) from the verb “sentar”. Often used with “por favor” or “sentem-se” (sit down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentem, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feel very cold in the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi sentenciado a dez anos de prisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to ten years in prison.

definitions.note: In everyday Portuguese, this most often means a grammatical sentence (in writing/speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa sentença está muito longa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sentence is very long.

definitions.note: In legal contexts, it refers to a judge’s decision (a ruling) or the punishment given by a court.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge read the ruling at the end of the trial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor corrigiu as sentenças do exercício.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher corrected the sentences from the exercise.

definitions.note: In legal contexts, “sentença” can mean a judge’s ruling or a punishment given by a court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O juiz leu as sentenças no final do julgamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge read the sentences at the end of the trial.

definitions.note: Usually used with "tu" (informal "you") in the present tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel cold at night?

definitions.note: past tense of "sentir" (most commonly "eu senti" = "I felt")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senti dor no braço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt pain in my arm.

definitions.native: felt, was feeling, used to feel
definitions.note: Imperfect past tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to feel afraid when I walked alone at night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t understand the meaning of the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta rua é de sentido único.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This street is one-way.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sentir" (used in compound tenses with "ter"/"haver").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu já tinha sentido isso antes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already felt that before.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the five senses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word has two meanings.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a strange feeling about that.

definitions.note: Plural of "sentimento".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't explain my feelings.

definitions.note: Present tense of "sentir" ("we" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentimos frio quando a janela fica aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We feel cold when the window stays open.

definitions.note: present participle / gerund of "sentir"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou me sentindo melhor hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm feeling better today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu consigo sentir a diferença.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel the difference.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can smell smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They felt very afraid during the storm.

definitions.note: Future tense (eu): “I will feel / I will hear.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will miss you.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will miss you.

definitions.note: Conditional (used for hypothetical situations).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would feel more confident if I practiced every day.

definitions.note: Conditional tense, 3rd person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles sentiriam mais confiança se tivessem mais tempo para praticar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would feel more confident if they had more time to practice.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of “sentir”.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "sentir"; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or conditions about the past (e.g., "se").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu sentisse dor, eu te avisaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I felt pain, I would let you know.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentiste medo quando ouviste aquele barulho?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you feel scared when you heard that noise?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of “sentir” (often used for a completed feeling in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sentiu medo quando ouviu o barulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt afraid when she heard the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sento aqui todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sit here every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “sentar” (to sit down).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat down on the chair and started to read.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to leave now, otherwise we'll miss the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vá agora, senão vamos perder o ônibus.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As toalhas estão separadas das roupas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The towels are separated from the clothes.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of "separar"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As duas equipes ficaram separadas durante o treino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two teams stayed separated during practice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os livros estão separados por assunto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are separated by subject.

definitions.note: Often used to describe marital/relationship status.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been separated for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos estão separados por categoria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents are separated by category.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles dormem em quartos separados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sleep in separate rooms.
